program: B3: Positivity certificates for counting sequences
scope: Results obtained from the attached snapshot. No original catalog or external ledger was modified.

status_policy.proved: A complete proof of the exact handoff statement is supplied and independently audited; not an assertion of publication priority.
status_policy.partial: A structural theorem settles a stated subcase or weaker property; full target remains unresolved.
status_policy.unresolved: Only scoped diagnostics, calibrations, instances, or reductions; no complete proof or counterexample to the exact target.

questions.question: Q164
questions.established: For every power of a path, domination counts are log-concave, including arbitrary nonnegative multiplicative vertex weights; more generally for interval-neighborhood graphs.
questions.limitations: Binomial-normalized ultra-log-concavity and the full cycle assertion remain unresolved.

questions.question: Q165
questions.established: For every n>=1 both parity polynomials have only real nonpositive roots. Stronger: D_Pn(x)/x^ceil(n/3) is strictly Hurwitz stable. An all-length positive generating-function recurrence proves coefficientwise nonnegativity of Re(D_n(iy)D_(n-1)(-iy)) as a polynomial in y^2.
questions.limitations: The zero polynomial component at n=1 is interpreted in the standard degenerate convention. Publication priority is unclaimed.

questions.question: Q166
questions.established: For every n>0 and ell>=2, compositions avoiding ell consecutive unit parts have log-concave counts by number of parts. The proof covers any interval-sum constraints on binary words and all fixed nonnegative position weights.
questions.limitations: Weighted conclusion is numerical for each weight choice, not coefficientwise log-concavity. Publication priority is unclaimed.

questions.question: Q167
questions.established: Complete all-integer classification, including every ordering compatible with ties, for n=1,2,3,4. Counts are 2,3,6,8; all orders have exact witnesses and exhaustiveness proofs.
questions.limitations: General degree n remains unresolved.

questions.question: Q183
questions.established: Every board with at most two rows or at most two columns has a real-rooted non-nesting rook polynomial, by a quadratic discriminant bound.
questions.limitations: Only an elementary control subclass. The entire forbidden-board avoidance class is unresolved.

questions.question: Q325
questions.established: All roots of every degree-d Stanley-nonnegative polynomial satisfy |Im z|<=B_d. For d>=2 equality forces real part -1/2 and a positive scalar multiple of M_d. Also a complete description of the attainable nonreal root locus by an explicit phase-span inequality.
questions.limitations: No canonical-line hypothesis. Publication priority is unclaimed.

questions.question: Q1158
questions.established: Every cycle-triangle minor of order at most two is nonnegative for every r>=1. Exact Neville factors certify all minors of the 25x25 blocks for r=2,3,11,12,16,32.
questions.limitations: Infinite minors of order at least three remain unresolved. Source already reports larger finite blocks for r<=10.

questions.question: Q1159
questions.established: Every subset-triangle minor of order at most two is nonnegative for every r>=1. Exact Neville factors certify all minors of the 25x25 blocks for r=2,3,11,12,16,32.
questions.limitations: Infinite minors of order at least three remain unresolved. Source already reports larger finite blocks for r<=10.

questions.question: Q1160
questions.established: For every r>=2 and every cycle Hankel minor on increasing nonnegative index sets I,J, the degree is sum(I)+sum(J), the vanishing order is |I|-1_{0 in I and 0 in J}, and both extreme coefficients are strictly positive.
questions.limitations: Interior coefficient positivity remains unresolved. A negative coefficient in a related subset Hankel minor is not a counterexample to this cycle question.

questions.question: Q1161
questions.established: Both third-order row families, for each n=1,...,80, have a simple zero at 0 and all other roots strictly in the left half-plane, certified by exact rational Routh pivots.
questions.limitations: No all-n stability proof. Failure of generic differential-operator stability preservation does not refute stability of the actual rows.

questions.question: Q1249
questions.established: An exact degree-seven candidate passes 300 genuine PF-input tests, covering 293 distinct generating functions. An explicit example shows that replacing PF inputs by merely log-concave inputs invalidates a tempting stronger claim.
questions.limitations: The all-input, all-remainder preservation conjecture remains unresolved. The stronger-claim failure is not a counterexample to Q1249.

questions.question: Q1262
questions.established: Finite recognition for arbitrary allowed vector length: enumerate ordered factorizations of N=p(1) with optional unit separators; length at most 2*Omega(N)-1 suffices. Complete exclusion for multiplicities (2,3). Infinite Pell family: A_(2,b)=E_(b-t+1,1,b+t+1) whenever b(b+1)/2=t^2. Exactly decided 28 bounded-volume uncolored two-symbol cases.
questions.limitations: A general structural classification of colored multiplicity pairs remains unresolved. The source already uses unit-removal and volume factorization in Proposition 25.

questions.question: Q1263
questions.established: Exact symmetric decomposition and gamma conversion implemented. Closed gamma formulas for two singleton symbols with color counts u,v>=2.
questions.limitations: No general combinatorial interpretation of both gamma vectors.

questions.question: Q1366
questions.established: All 200523 classical-pattern intervals with nonempty bottom and top length<=7 are unimodal; 206436 if the empty bottom is included. Literal subset enumeration independently checks downsets through length5.
questions.limitations: The infinite interval conjecture remains unresolved. The rank vector (1,2,5,5,1) is a log-concavity failure, not a unimodality failure.

questions.question: Q1441
questions.established: r_2=(1+sqrt(2))/2. The bounds r_n>=5/4 for every even n>=6 and r_n>=51/40 for every even n>=16 follow from exact Sturm-certified bases and product closure.
questions.limitations: No upper bound independent of n is proved; the uniform-boundedness question remains unresolved.

questions.question: Q1442
questions.established: R_2=2 and R_3=3. Complete degree-two root locus. All fixed-degree interpolation extrema are attained after normalization; their imaginary extent is strictly below the corresponding SNN bound for degrees>=2.
questions.limitations: R_n=n for n>=4 remains unresolved.

questions.question: Q1443
questions.established: The polynomial (5z^2+5z-2)^12 belongs to U_24 by exact Sturm certification and has consecutive distinct real-root gap sqrt(13/5). Thus any universal gap bound is at least sqrt(13/5).
questions.limitations: Does not disprove or prove existence of a bound below 2.

questions.question: Q1454
questions.established: Known Catalan and finite-atomic moment cases supply explicit nonnegative measures and exact PSD/rank controls for the toolkit.
questions.limitations: No general principal-pattern avoidance moment theorem. These are calibration cases, not claimed new family results.

questions.question: Q2212
questions.established: Exhaustive over every numerical monoid for every cutoff ell=0,...,22: all atom-count rows are unimodal and in fact log-concave. At ell=22 there are 7257 possible truncations. Independent literal-set verification through ell=8.
questions.limitations: No conclusion for ell>=23. Clarified that the cited almost-unimodality result concerns most positions within a row, not almost every cutoff.

questions.question: Q2400
questions.established: For fixed d>0 and n>=max(2,d), simultaneously x_k^2>=x_(k-1)x_(k+1) for 1<=k<=min(n-1,floor(((n-1)/(2d))^(1/3))) with probability at least 1-exp(-d(n-1)/6). Also an exact positive expectation formula for every defect.
questions.limitations: The full coefficient row with high probability remains unresolved. Positive expectation alone does not imply a high-probability sign.
